interface.name: caminito_intellihide_manager_v1

description.summary: ask for intellihide on a layer surface

interface.description:
A client that has a panel on a layer surface can ask the compositor for intellihide: the compositor hides the surface off its edge while a window on its output's active workspace overlaps it, and shows it when none does, or when the pointer rests at that edge. The compositor knows every window's geometry, which a client doesn't, so it decides, and it moves the surface itself.
The client is never told that its surface is hidden. It draws as usual, and the surface's input region goes with it. A client that wants intellihide should not reserve space with an exclusive zone, since a surface that hides can't keep it.
This is a private protocol of Caminito's. A client that finds no global does nothing, and its surface stays where it is.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the layer surface already has an intellihide object

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the manager. Intellihide objects it made are not affected.

request.name: get_intellihide

description.summary: ask for intellihide on a layer surface

request.description:
Asks for intellihide on the layer surface, from now until the returned object is destroyed or the layer surface is. The compositor changes nothing else of the layer surface: its layer, anchors, margins and exclusive zone are the client's. The edge it hides off is the one the surface is anchored to; a surface anchored to no single edge is not hidden.
It is a protocol error to make a second object for one layer surface.

interface.name: caminito_intellihide_v1

description.summary: a layer surface that asks for intellihide

interface.description: The existence of this object is the request: a layer surface with one is hidden and shown by the compositor, and one without is an ordinary layer surface. There are no events.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The layer surface is shown where it is and stays there, as an ordinary layer surface does.
